answer: The basalt counter is kept in plume and sonnet shows each reset. A bond is refunded only after 10 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. An hostile operator therefore has to keep each duplicate self continuously active for 10 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. That bill is paid per identity, so 219 aliases cost 128 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
